senses.gloss: small dealer, retailer in the market, huckster, contrad. to פלטר shop-keeper.
units: <cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Shekalim 8:1:3">Y. Shek. VIII, beg. 51ᵃ</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="Deuteronomy 28:66">Deut. XXVIII, 66</cite>) <he>ופחדת … זה שהוא לוקח מן הס׳ וכ׳</he> ‘and thou shalt be in fear day and night’, that is, he who buys from the huckster (who cannot lay in stock for a year), ‘and thou shalt have no assurance of thy life’—that is, he who buys from the shop-keeper; ib. III, 47ᶜ <cite ref="R00327"><he>ציוקי</he></cite> (corr. acc.); <cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat 8:1:9">Y. Sabb. VIII, 11ᵃ</cite> bot.; Esth. R. introd., beg.; a. fr.
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Nedarim 11:2:2">Y. Ned. XI, 42ᶜ</cite> bot. <he>והיו שם צבורים בס׳</he> and there were provisions piled up in the market.

<cite ref="Ruth Rabbah, Petichta 1">Ruth R. to I, 1</cite> <he>יצתה ועומדת בס׳ …</he> (not <he>מעילת</he>) his maid servant went out and stood in the market (waiting for her turn to buy provision); <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Nach 598">Yalk. Ruth 598</cite>.

<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Demai 3:4:2">Y. Dem. III, 23ᶜ</cite> <he>ס׳ שהיתה מסתפקת וכ׳</he> a provision stand which was supplied with forbidden fruits one day; ib. II, 22ᶜ top <cite ref="K00383"><he>כורכיא</he></cite> (corr. acc.); Y. Keth. I, 25ᵈ bot. (<cite ref="O01613"><he>סִירְ׳</he></cite>) <cite ref="O00585"><he>סִידְקִית</he></cite>; a. fr.—
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Kilayim 2:1:4">Y. Kil. II, beg. 27ᶜ</cite> (in Chald. dict.) <he>בסירקי</he> in the market-stand.
